In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the quality of language models, by making them better at capturing factual knowledge.
the problem of incorporating knowledge in pretrained transformers without changing the architecture, and without adding explicit knowledge storage.
the question: can language models be pre-trained to be aware of the world around them?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work is a first step in the direction of incorporating knowledge in language modeling pretraining, and that it is an important step in the direction.
\kalm{} is the best of the three models for all tasks, with a clear margin in some cases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can make the transformer more knowledge-aware by simply signaling the existence of entities at the input and output of the model, with a simple tokenizer and a knowledge prediction task.
we are trying to make the language models more aware of the entities in the language and the world.

by adding a simple entity signal to the pretraining process, we are able to significantly improve the factual and semantic correctness of language model parameters without changing the transformer model architecture or adding external knowledge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a language model can be made knowledge-aware by simply adding entity signals in pre-training, with no additional architecture changes.

the transformer architecture is a powerful knowledge model, and that it is sufficient to simply signal the presence of entities in the input and output to the transformer during pretraining to improve its knowledge-awareness.
transformers are not as knowledge-agnostic as previously assumed.
